title: Bluff Point topobathy patch (active bluff landslides west of Homer), 2 m
note: Messy-data patch (Hig, 2026-10-15): real ground change between the 2008, 2018 and 2019 lidars on the Bluff Point slide complex, a green-lidar strip (Homer 2018 NCMP) across the intertidal, and three bathymetries of different quality offshore (H12146 multibeam, the 2023 NOAA OCM satellite-derived 2 m grid, the NCEI 1/3 arc-second 2010 grid). Nothing is tuned to the site: the time axis does the work (rates.ground 0.05 m/yr says this ground moves, so a newer survey outranks an older one even at equal sigma, and lowest is off because a lower surface here is change, not canopy). Box x 572-580 km, y 6609-6617 km, 2 m. First pass; see TOPOBATHY_REVIEW.md section 7.
rates_notes: ground 0.05 m/yr (default 0.01): an active landslide coast -- the surveys differ by real change, so age must count against an observation. bed 0.05: a mobile sandy nearshore.

layers.name: ctx3dep
layers.notes: USGS 3DEP 1/3 arc-second fallback, shown only where no survey has a cell. water_3dep.tif (topobathy/flat_water.py, built by the chain): 3DEP's hydroflattened lakes as water, so a lake outside every survey gets a basin and 3DEP never stands as ground inside one.

layers.name: ncei2010
layers.notes: NCEI Kachemak Bay 1/3 arc-second (~10 m) 2010 grid, MHW; +3.91 m to NAVD88 measured against Hydropalooza (bathy_src/outer_kachemak/README.md). Bed only below MLLW (-1.38 m NAVD88): its land is poor and never used. A gridded prior: void inside the intertidal zone (tidal lens, 2026-10-16).

layers.name: ocm2023
layers.date_note: published 2023; its bathymetry here is the 2018/2019 green lidar plus interpolation (DPR: 81 % GMT surface), and a conditioned prior must not post-date its references
layers.notes: NOAA OCM 2023 seamless topobathy 2 m, NAVD88, read from the -novshift warp in cmp_ocm (the original's compound CRS trips the gdalwarp geoid shift). Satellite-derived bathymetry in the shallows (NMAD 0.17 m vs Hydropalooza at 5-20 m, 0.47 beyond): sigma 1.0 so any lidar or multibeam outranks it. Bed only below MLLW: its land is 2008 lidar / IfSAR, not an observation of 2023. A gridded prior: void inside the intertidal zone (tidal lens, 2026-10-16).

layers.name: bathy2009
layers.notes: Hydropalooza multibeam, already NAVD88 (-1.38 m MLLW shift in the archive).

layers.name: h12146
layers.notes: NOAA survey H12146 BAG (MODE=INTERPOLATED extract), MLLW -> NAVD88 by the collection's -1.38 m; agrees with Hydropalooza to 0.00 (0.003) on their 11 km2 overlap. Survey date assumed 2010 (H121xx numbering); the BAG's own datetime is its 2021 export.

layers.name: kenai2008
layers.notes: Kenai 2008 (NOAA/NGS IOCM, our rebuild from the USGS points, NAVD88). Ground only: no water class in the USGS copy; the sea is a hole or absent. water_level (2026-10-16, Hig's v7 review): its returns off the sea at the 2008 tide are water, not ground -- a 150 m round spot of them 300 m off Bluff Point stood 2.5 m proud of the bed as 'ground'. islets (2026-10-16, Bluff Point lump): specks of ground under 200 m2 ringed by water/void/bed are returns off the sea surface, classed water. 2026-10-18: water from the point cloud (topobathy/water_taught.py on observe_points.py cellstats: density, intensity, roughness, level, height above the local bottom; taught on mapped lakes, deep seabed and high ground; held-out lake precision 0.97, recall 0.90).

layers.name: homer2018
layers.notes: USACE NCMP 2018 topobathy (green lidar) bare earth, 0.54 m: bed below MLLW, ground above (the intertidal is ground at low tide and is what the composite wants there). flat_lakes (2026-10-15): a ground patch flat to 3 cm over 14 m, >= 2000 m2, lower than 60 % of a 10 m ring by 0.1 m, is water at its level (the lakes with no water returns, TOPOBATHY_REVIEW 8.1). islets (2026-10-16, Bluff Point lump): specks of ground under 200 m2 ringed by water/void/bed are returns off the sea surface, classed water. flat_below (2026-10-16, Bluff Point): the green lidar returns the sea surface at its flight tide (-1.6..-0.5 m) as a smooth sheet, which below_level split into bed and ground; a flat sheet below 0 m NAVD88 is water, whether below_level called it bed or ground (so it runs after below_level, on every class). facets (2026-10-18): the vendor DTM bridges its data gaps with a TIN; cells planar to 2 cm over 10 m in patches of 200 m2 or more are "modelled", not ground (Beluga Lake south corner: Homer 2019 0.7-4 m above the 2018 surface across a gap).

layers.name: homer2019
layers.notes: DGGS RDF 2021-2 DTM (not the hydro-flattened one), 0.5 m. Water where flat at the grid's modal sea level (pinned by the pre-pass), if the DTM holds the sea at all; its point cloud is 85/171 tiles readable (TOPOBATHY_REVIEW.md 7), so no point classes yet. flat_lakes (2026-10-15): a ground patch flat to 3 cm over 14 m, >= 2000 m2, lower than 60 % of a 10 m ring by 0.1 m, is water at its level (the lakes with no water returns, TOPOBATHY_REVIEW 8.1). facets (2026-10-18): the vendor DTM bridges its data gaps with a TIN; cells planar to 2 cm over 10 m in patches of 200 m2 or more are "modelled", not ground (Beluga Lake south corner: Homer 2019 0.7-4 m above the 2018 surface across a gap).

fill.notes: low_tide_m = MLLW in NAVD88 (-1.38 m, the collection's measured value), not a flight-day tide. tidal_lens (default): marine domains take the observed water surface as the bed, no low-tide floor, no channel by width; measured beds under it (multibeam, green-lidar returns, soundings) still condition it.

water.notes: stage B (topobathy/water.py): per-survey water observations and bodies; a lake's or a perched lagoon's own level is the bed cutoff in the below_level steps (bodies: $out/), and the fill takes the body's kind. Chain: build --diag -> water -> build -> fill -> build. Tidal lens (Hig, 2026-10-16): water the tide reaches (kinds sea/tidal/perched) is a flat at its observed surface until measured; intertidal.tif = those bodies + within intertidal_near_m of ground/water observed between the fill's low_tide_m and tide_max_m, where the priors (ncei2010, ocm2023) are void.
water.mapped_notes: Hig's hand-mapped lakes (water/sources.json): a prior for the flat-lake detector (inside a mapped polygon: min area 100 m2, no ring test), islands for the hole rule, and the mapped-vs-bodies report; never a stamp.
